book: Book generation: delegate the actual generation run to `codex` (or `gemini` if codex is unavailable) per the standing implementation-delegation rule -- don't hand-write book content yourself when a run can be scripted. Canonical binary: ~/Dev/BookFactory/book-factory-v13/bookfactoryv13 (build with `go build .` in that dir if the binary is missing) -- it's a superset of v12, same flags plus --curate. Flags on `run`: --topic "<idea>" (required, free text) plus one of: --facts <file> for citation-honest nonfiction (constrains prose to the supplied research, requires a confidence tag -- primary_source/secondary_source/general_inference/unresolved_gap -- on every citation-bearing claim, never invents a source); --fictionalize <file> for real-event-inspired fiction (obscures real people/orgs from the facts file into fictional substitutes before writing, then emits a similarity_report.md flagging any leaked real names or clustered identifying details -- that report is a heuristic aid, not legal clearance, real/identifiable-person content still needs human review before publishing); --curate <file> for quote/source-anthology books (source file is repeated `> "quote"` blocks each followed by an — Attribution line, blank-line separated; model only selects/arranges quotes and writes connective commentary, the program substitutes the real on-disk quote text back in so it can't drift or get paraphrased, and a curation_report.md verifies byte-for-byte fidelity -- that report confirms quotes weren't altered, not that reproducing them is cleared for publication, still needs human review for permissions/fair-use); --append <chapter.md> to extend an existing chapter/catalog file in its own format instead of generating a fresh manuscript (the right mode for a catalog-style book built up over many runs, one entry/section at a time); --code-disciplines for fixed decision-formula articles with code. Plain --topic alone (no other flag) is for pure fiction or breezy trade nonfiction where no external facts are being constrained or transformed. Older versions (v5-v12) exist for reference/backward compatibility only -- v13 is where new capability lands; don't fork a v14 for a new book kind, add a flag to v13 instead unless the user explicitly asks for a fork (v13 itself was a user-requested exception to that rule, not the new default pattern).
